record.paper_title: Some open problems concerning the convergence of positive series
record.original_question: Let A be a set of integers such that the reciprocal series sum_{n in A} 1/n diverges. Is it true that A contains arithmetic progressions of arbitrarily large finite length? In particular, must A contain at least one arithmetic progression of length three?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. (P. Erdös). If the sum of reciprocals of a set A of integers diverges, then that set contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
This conjecture is still open even if one only seeks a single progression of length three.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a set of positive integers such that the series of reciprocals
  ∑_{n ∈ A} 1/n
diverges. Prove or disprove the following statement: for every integer k ≥ 3, the set A contains a non-trivial arithmetic progression of length k, i.e., there exist a ∈ ℤ and d ∈ ℤ_{>0} such that a, a+d, a+2d, …, a+(k−1)d all belong to A. In particular, settle the case k = 3 (must A contain at least one three-term arithmetic progression?) and the general case of arbitrarily large k.
artifact.status_search_result: The case k = 3 of the Erdős conjecture was resolved by Bloom and Sisask (2020), who proved that any subset of {1,…,N} avoiding non-trivial three-term arithmetic progressions has size O(N/(log N)^{1+c}), which implies that any set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum must contain a 3-term progression. The general conjecture (arithmetic progressions of arbitrary length k ≥ 4) remains open.

status_evidence.title: Erdős conjecture on arithmetic progressions - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Bloom and Sisask proved the first non-trivial case of the conjecture, showing the three-term case holds.
status_evidence.claim: The k=3 case is solved; the general conjecture is open.

status_evidence.title: Landmark Math Proof Clears Hurdle in Top Erdős Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Bloom and Sisask proved that any set whose reciprocals form a divergent series must contain 3-term arithmetic progressions.
